description: Steady B1 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Velvet has /ɛ/ in its first syllable. Valid has /æ/, village has /ɪ/, and volume has /ɑ/ in General American.
Seldom has /ɛ/ in its first syllable. Salmon and solemn begin with /æ/ and /ɑ/ respectively in General American, while sullen has /ʌ/.
Flutter has /ʌ/ in its first syllable. Flatter has /æ/, flitter has /ɪ/, and fluter is not the standard spelling of the common word.
Genre begins with /ʒ/ in General American. Gentry and genuine begin with /dʒ/, while general begins with /dʒ/.
Wren begins with /r/ because the written w is silent. Rent also begins with /r/ but has a pronounced final /t/; when begins with /w/ and then with /ð/.
Xylophone begins with /z/, the sound of initial x in this word. Sylvan begins with /s/, pterodactyl with /t/ because p is silent, and pharmacy with /f/.
Mixed ends with the consonant cluster /kst/. Mix ends with /ks/, mist with /st/, and midst with /dst/.
Judged ends with /dʒd/ in careful General American pronunciation. Judge ends with /dʒ/, jugs with /ɡz/, and jungle with /ɡəl/.
Strength ends with /ŋθ/. String ends with /ŋ/, strange with /ndʒ/, and strenth is not a standard spelling.
Doubtful keeps the silent b in doubt before adding -ful. The other options are misspellings.
Mission uses ssion to spell the /ʃən/ ending. The other options are not standard spellings.
Foreign is spelled f-o-r-e-i-g-n; the i comes before the g. The other options use incorrect letter order or omit a letter.
